TODO

Source: TODO.md

Findings from the code review of R/ (2026-11-06). Ordered by priority. None of these are blocking.

0. Release housekeeping for the pending changes

  • Run the full test suite and devtools::check() before committing; only the NEC, ED, maED, mselect and related test files were run after the NEC edfct change.

1. Make drmEMstandard (responses relative to control) a supported analysis type

Purpose (confirmed): GLS for data expressed relative to the control mean (e.g. % of control), where all observations share the estimated control mean and are therefore correlated. Today it is an unreachable prototype (not wired into drm(), wrong covariance for the control rows, no multi-curve support, wrong log-likelihood). Detailed plan: .build_artifacts/2026-11-09_drmEMstandard_implementation_plan.md (start with Phase -1 baseline and Phase 0 statistics; six open questions at the end of the plan need an answer first).

Do not remove R/drmEMstandard.R, tests/testthat/test-drmEMstandard.R or the "standard" branches in rse() and vcov.drc().

2. Guard against NAMESPACE drift (process, not a bug)

NAMESPACE is hand-maintained (no roxygen header), so @export tags are ignored by devtools::document() for it.

  • Whenever you add an exported function or S3 method, edit NAMESPACE by hand in the same commit.
  • Before each release run devtools::check() and look for “Undocumented code objects” and “S3 methods not registered” notes.
  • Optional: add a test that compares getNamespaceExports("drc") to a stored list so unintended export changes fail CI.

3. Quieten redundant SE warnings when ED is NA (minor)

ED() on a fit where edfct returns NA (e.g. NEC with an out-of-range level) prints the new, specific warning plus two generic “Non-positive variance estimate; SE set to NA.” warnings from the SE step in ED.drc. Skip the SE computation (or its warning) when the ED estimate is not finite.

4. Remaining models without edfct (feature gap)

ED() still stops for baro5, CRS.6, gammadr, gompertzd, hewlett, ursa, voelund, twophase and threephase (edfct <- NULL). Decide per model whether a closed-form or uniroot based edfct is meaningful (the mixture models hewlett/ursa/voelund probably not), and document the ones that stay unsupported.
